title: Anyone’s kids vibe coding or making games?
author: ghostly-blossom
selftext:
My 13 year old son used to make these Roblox games and take hours just to get one tiny thing perfect. I let him use my codex and he built a game where you build a car with swords and run things over. 

Are there any apps or things my son should look into? I saw there was some Roblox vibe coding videos? Any YouTubers or TikTok creators worth following that explains things a 13 year old can understand?

Thank you

comments.author: Brewgazer
comments.body: Get him a $20 subscription to cursor and let him go nuts, tell him to ask a free chat gpt type ai what language to build in and the best practices for vibecoding in game development

replies.author: Fun_Ebb_2763
replies.body: Why cursor? Why not just chatgpt or better yet Claude?

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Because cursors base models you get from them you get an abundance of usage and you also get clause usage as well as gpt models, this give the kid the chance to use something that’ll eat usage like crazy but then have the base models to use when they use up the extra api usage. Grok 4.6 can do a bunch especially when given skills to utilize

replies.author: ghostly-blossom
replies.body: Appreciate it. I haven’t checked out cursor but will take a look

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Honestly it’s really great for beginners and those who understand adding skills and using outside tools

comments.author: god-damn-the-usa
comments.body:
godot is a great free game engine, and typically works pretty well with vibe coding (especially with the godot-ai mcp for testing).

ideally you get him a subscription to claude or codex

replies.author: ghostly-blossom
replies.body: Thanks! He did make the game on godot, just Roblox style

replies.author: ScalpM3
replies.body: Use freebuff or something first before you pay any subscriptions, that way he can use DeepSeek or gtp 5.6 for 6 hours a day free

comments.author: ZerkyXii
comments.body: You should like not let him use AI if you want him to learn

replies.author: eckstuhc
replies.body: You should also not let him use a compiler if you want him to really learn

replies.author: ZerkyXii
replies.body: Literally big difference compiling code versus having a AI writing the whole thing and not learning anything. Wild

replies.author: iamjohncarterofmars
replies.body:
What if he’s not trying to learn and just wants to screw around and have fun making random shit?

Fun police over here 🙄

replies.author: ZerkyXii
replies.body: I said if you want him to learn dont use AI though did I say otherwise?

replies.author: iamjohncarterofmars
replies.body:
No, but then I don’t see the utility in your comment at all

OP didn’t say they wanted their kid to get formal lessons on coding

replies.author: ZerkyXii
replies.body: Sorry should've said why use tiktok or youtube when you can ask the ai how to use the ai. There you go

replies.author: ghostly-blossom
replies.body:
Thanks. My son plays on a sports team, has two music programs, and honors classes. He gets up, goes to school, practice, comes home around 7pm, exhausted. 

Truly, god forbid he wants to make himself something cool.

replies.author: iamjohncarterofmars
replies.body:
I’ve made tons of little games too!! It’s really a fun way to kill time when you get into a project hahaha

I think sticking with your codex or even getting him his own ChatGPT Go or Plus account would be the best move for now. OpenAI has frontier models that are on par or almost on par with the likes of Anthropic’s Fable and Opus lines. But the real benefit is that ChatGPT gives tremendous usage limits for a fraction of the cost of Claude. If your son has a .edu email, there is a free $100 codex credit promo going on

replies.author: Spudly42
replies.body: It's an interesting point.  As a parent, maybe you could encourage them to learn as they go.  Try to get them to explain the architecture of the game and explain why they made different choices and what it.  Even if it was the AI that chose, you still learn if you understand why they made the choice (which basically just means read what the AI writes and think about it).

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: NoahLR
comments.body: Summer Engine is the most intuitive experience I've tried so far

comments.author: Embarrassed_Run_1238
comments.body: the car with swords game sounds sick. honestly at 13 just let him keep at it and have him ask the ai "how do i do x" instead of tutorials

replies.author: ghostly-blossom
replies.body: That is a skill I really want him to have (learning to ask the ai better questions). I noticed his generation, even the honors kids, struggle with asking precise questions or describing with specificity and it showed in the way he used ChatGPT.

comments.author: SharksFan1
comments.body: My 11 year old has made some Minecraft mods
